property_summary: After a pool calls mintSynth(member,amount), the pool's recorded LP collateral balance (as observed by getmapAddress_LPBalance) increases by at least the LP units deposited during that call.
Calls to mintSynth from a pool should never revert for any positive amount when the pool has newly deposited LP tokens (i.e., when added LP > 0).
The test asserts that calling c.mintSynth(member, amount) with amount>0 does not revert (i.e., reverted == false).
On the original contract P, mintSynth called by a curated pool that already has a positive recorded LP balance should not revert for any positive amount.
Calling c.mintSynth(member, amount) with amount > 0 from an address that currently has a positive recorded LP balance in C does not revert on the original contract.

For any caller and pool address, calling allowance(...) is a view that does not modify synth LP bookkeeping: after calling allowance on C, mapSynth_LPBalance[pool] remains equal to its prior value; the mutant that omits crediting mapSynth_LPBalance in mintSynth can cause mapSynth_LPBalance to differ after interactions (the fuzzer will trigger via a prior mintSynth call), so the reference preserves balances while the mutant can show a mismatch.

For any pool address p and any mint amount, calling allowance(...) (a read-only call) does not change C.mapSynth_LPBalance(p) in the reference implementation, but the mutant (which fails to credit mapSynth_LPBalance in mintSynth) can make mapSynth_LPBalance diverge from expected values after a sequence that includes mintSynth, so the invariant that allowance(...) never changes mapSynth_LPBalance(p) for any p holds in the reference and is broken by the mutant for some inputs.

Calling the view allowance(...) never changes any mapSynth_LPBalance[p] in the correct contract, but the mutant (which fails to credit mapSynth_LPBalance in mintSynth) can make that mapping differ after sequences involving mintSynth, so the invariant 'allowance is a read-only call w.r.t. mapSynth_LPBalance' holds for the reference and is violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs.

Calling the view function allowance(...) does not modify any mapSynth_LPBalance[pool] in the correct contract for any input; the mutant that omits crediting mapSynth_LPBalance inside mintSynth can produce sequences where mapSynth_LPBalance differs (so the allowance call should leave mapSynth_LPBalance unchanged but the mutant leads to differing values for some fuzz inputs).

For any addresses a,b and any prior minting activity, calling allowance(a,b) is a read-only operation that does not change any mapSynth_LPBalance(key) in the correct contract; the mutant (which fails to credit mapSynth_LPBalance in mintSynth) allows a sequence where mapSynth_LPBalance for some pool differs after such interactions, so the invariant that allowance() leaves mapSynth_LPBalance unchanged is violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs.

After a pool calls mintSynth with some LP added, the pool's recorded LP balance increase equals the synthetic debt increase (mapSynth_LPBalance[pool] - previous == mapSynth_LPDebt[pool] - previousDebt) — i.e., LP units credited equals synth amount minted proportionally, so the increment in LP balance equals the increment in LP-debt when starting from zero debt/balance.
Calls to mintSynth from any pool should never revert (i.e., succeed) when the caller is a curated pool and the pool has added LP tokens (lpUnits>0).
When amount>0 and member is nonzero, calling c.mintSynth(member, amount) must not revert (i.e., reverted == false).
When the precondition holds, calling c.mintSynth(member, amount) must not revert (reverted == false).
When amount>0 and member is nonzero and msg.sender already has a positive recorded LP balance in c, calling c.mintSynth(member, amount) must not revert.

For any pool address p and minted amount, calling C.allowance(...) does not modify mapSynth_LPBalance(p) in the correct contract; the mutant that doubles-credit LP balance causes mapSynth_LPBalance(p) to be larger for some inputs after interactions that trigger mintSynth, so observing mapSynth_LPBalance after allowance can differ between reference and mutant.

Calling allowance(address,uint) is a view that must not change mapSynth_LPBalance for any pool in the correct contract; the mutant's incorrect mintSynth (which double-credits LP balance) can cause mapSynth_LPBalance(k) to differ after allowance-driven interactions for some fuzzed inputs.

Calling the view function allowance(address owner, address spender) never changes any mapSynth_LPBalance(key) in the correct contract, while the mutant (which doubles mapSynth_LPBalance on mintSynth) can cause mapSynth_LPBalance(somePool) to be different after an interaction sequence that performs a mint; thus for all inputs allowance leaves mapSynth_LPBalance unchanged in the reference, but the mutant yields a larger mapSynth_LPBalance for some fuzzed inputs.

Calling allowance(...) (a view) does not change any mapSynth_LPBalance(key) in the correct contract for any sequence of inputs; the mutant that double-credits mapSynth_LPBalance during mintSynth can lead to some inputs (when a pool performs mintSynth) where mapSynth_LPBalance(key) is larger after the same sequence, so the invariant that allowance leaves mapSynth_LPBalance unchanged is violated by the mutant.

Calling the view function allowance(owner,spender) never mutates any mapSynth_LPBalance(key) in the correct contract; the mutant that double-credits mapSynth_LPBalance during mintSynth can cause mapSynth_LPBalance(somePool) to be larger after the same sequence of external interactions, so the invariant 'allowance does not change mapSynth_LPBalance(k)' holds for all inputs on reference but is violated by the mutant for some fuzzed inputs.
Only addresses that are curated pools (isCuratedPool == true) can call mintSynth on C, so mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender] increases after mintSynth; non-curated callers cannot increase that balance.
